title: Systems of Linear Inequalities
seo_title: Algebra II Systems of Linear Inequalities Worksheets (TEKS 2A.3E–2A.3G)
standard_text: 2A.3E formulate systems of at least two linear inequalities in two variables; 2A.3F solve systems of two or more linear inequalities in two variables; 2A.3G determine possible solutions in the solution set of systems of two or more linear inequalities in two variables
meta_desc: Free Algebra II worksheets on systems of linear inequalities for Texas TEKS 2A.3E to 2A.3G: graphs, test points, writing systems from words and possible solutions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A solution makes every inequality true.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The solution of a system of inequalities is the region where all the shadings overlap.
  • A point is a solution only if it makes every inequality true.
  • “At most” means ≤; “at least” means ≥; “more than” means >.
  • In real situations, add x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0, and keep whole numbers for things you count.

Examples

Example

Is (2, 1) a solution of y ≤ x, y > −1, x < 4?

1 ≤ 2 ✓

1 > −1 ✓

2 < 4 ✓

Answer: Yes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reversing at least and at mostAt least 20 means ≥ 20.
Testing only one inequalityTest every inequality.
Swapping the pricesEach price goes with its own variable.

faq.q: Is a point on a dashed line a solution?
faq.a: No. Dashed lines (< or >) are not included.

items.q: A club sells x cookies for $15 each and y brownies for $2 each. It can bake at most 30 items and wants to earn at least $740. Which system describes this situation (with x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0)?
